DIM-WEIGHT-ROUNDS-UP/F1.why: Dimensional weight rounds down; tests/test_parcel.py fails by assertion (unittest failure) in all three runs.

DIM-WEIGHT-ROUNDS-UP/F2.why: Height is replaced by width; the dimensional-weight assertions fail in all three runs.

STANDARD-BASE-RATE/F1.why: Every rate gains one extra step; assertions fail in all three runs.

STANDARD-BASE-RATE/F2.why: Zone 3's step price changes; the zone-3 assertions fail in all three runs.

EXPRESS-RATE-AND-LIMIT/F1.why: The half-cent rounding is dropped; the express assertions fail in all three runs.

EXPRESS-RATE-AND-LIMIT/F2.why: Parcels over the express limit are accepted; the assertRaises checks fail in all three runs.

REMOTE-SURCHARGE/F1.why: Part of the remote postal range is lost; the boundary assertions fail in all three runs.

REMOTE-SURCHARGE/F2.why: Express remote deliveries are charged the standard surcharge; assertions fail in all three runs.

OVERSIZE-SURCHARGE-CLASSES/F1.why: tests/test_surcharges.py never tests oversize (partial): green 3/3. Control (surcharges.py unparseable) fails to load, so the defender imports the module. The whole suite 3/3: no test fails in every run (oversize is not checked anywhere).

TRACKING-NUMBER-FORMAT/F1.why: The sequence upper bound drops a digit; the tests that build the largest valid tracking number now get ValueError raised outside assertRaises, an error (exception) in all three runs and no assertion failure.

changed.why: Selections derived by reading the imports (spec: a changed path selects a claim when it is a fault target, a defender, or in the import closure of either). Every test imports the shipping package, whose __init__ imports every module, so any change under shipping/ reaches every claim. The working tree also holds build/lib/shipping and build/lib/fieldkit, untracked and git-ignored copies (a build directory, #272; fieldkit resolves its submodules by computed import): no test imports them and no change to them can be committed.
